test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 14 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The lawyer said, "Your case is very complicated."

options.text: The lawyer said that my case was very complicated.
The lawyer reported that my case is very complicated.
The lawyer said that my case had been very complicated.
The lawyer warned that your case was very complicated.

solution:
The correct sentence is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **indirect speech,** when reporting or narrating someone else's words, we typically shift the tense back one step into the past.
 
• Therefore, **the verb** **"is"** in the original direct speech changes to** "was" **in the indirect form to maintain the past tense.
 
• The **structure of indirect speech **in this case is: Reporting verb (said) + that + subject + past tense of the verb (was) + rest of the sentence.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *The lawyer said that my case was very complicated. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2,** "The lawyer reported that my case is very complicated," is not correct because it does not reflect the shift of tense required in indirect speech. It uses the present tense "is" instead of the past tense "was."
 
• **Option 3,** "The lawyer said that my case had been very complicated," is also not correct. It uses the past perfect tense ("had been") which is not necessary in this context, as the original sentence is already in the present tense.
 
• **Option 4**, "The lawyer warned that your case was very complicated," changes the meaning of the original sentence. It introduces the verb "warned" instead of "said," which alters the intention of the lawyer's statement.
